finding.issue: A distinct-local bound alone does not bound repeated recursive traversal of a shared acyclic Phi DAG.
finding.example: Each successive merge Phi refers to the previous merge local on both predecessor edges. Each visit repeats the complete prior proof. With n Phi nodes and one root Move, visits grow as 2^(n+1)-1 while distinct locals grow as n+1.
finding.required_fix: Fail closed after 256 total ProveAt visits per proof, retaining per-use availability checks.
finding.production_fixture_expectation: Short shared Phi DAG accepted; larger valid shared DAG rejected at the total visit budget.

checked_contracts: SsaForm inserts Phi sources in the exact positional order of Block.Predecessors; the proof uses that same order and checks definition availability at each predecessor end.
Exact predecessor arity, leading Phi/Nop prefix, unique SSA definition, same-block instruction ordering and fresh cross-block dominance are checked.
Unique reachable reciprocal topology is validated before dominance construction; unreachable non-exit blocks and dangling, asymmetric or duplicate edges reject.
Each traversed local must retain the exact represented TypeAnalysisContext identity through Move roots; propagated names or RuntimeClass typing alone do not suffice.
Active dependency cycles reject; acyclic metadata values reused on loop paths may pass only when their definitions are available on every edge.
Taking a traversed class local address anywhere conservatively rejects that origin. Address wrappers nested through supported memory and index operands are inspected.
The non-Phi Move path retains unique-definition and availability checks and receives conservative whole-graph topology and address-escape checks.
The proof changes class identity eligibility only; existing helper ABI, unused-result, closed-type and exact RuntimeHelpers overload gates remain.
